newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia mines ministry delays Bre-X contract.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mines ministry delays Bre-X contract.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Ministry is delaying issuing a contract of work to Canadian gold company Bre-X Minerals Ltd until a dispute with Indonesian partners is resolved, Director-General of Mining Kuntoro Mangkusubroto said on Thursday.
Bre-X has applied for a COW for the Busang II and Busang III areas (Blocks B and C) covering a massive deposit of gold in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province.
The company has estimated gold reserves in the deposit of at least 47 million ounces.
Industry sources said the dispute centres on claims by an Indonesian partner in the Busang I (Block A) area for a 10-percent stake in the other two areas.
The sources said Bre-X about two years ago bought the Busang I property between Busang II and Busang III from Australian company PT Westralian Atan Minerals.
Also involved in the original block A were two local partners.

The sources said one of the two had staked several claims through mining permits, available only to Indonesians, outside Blocks B and C. He then entered into a joint venture agreement with Bre-X, which applied for COWs for Blocks B and C.

The other partner in Block A, however, is also claiming a 10-percent share in the two other blocks, which hold the bulk of the gold deposit. Bre-X disputes his claim, and has quoted its Indonesian legal adviser as saying it was without merit.
Bre-X has estimated the gold reserves in Block A at around three million ounces. It said the richest deposit was in Block B.
Lack of a contract of work restricts Bre-X from further development of the deposit. It has estimated a mine will require an investment of around $1.0 billion.
The Bre-X office in Jakarta refused all comment, referring queries to its office in Toronto.
